outcome: No result addressing the strong (convex) Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture was found in the window; it remains open, and only the pre-2024 resolution of the weaker non-convex version, and pre-2024 partial/area results on the convex version, exist.
summary: The strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture (every polyhedral graph has a planar greedy embedding with all faces convex) is distinct from the original (weak) Papadimitriou–Ratajczak / greedy embedding conjecture, which was resolved positively by Leighton and Moitra in 2008/2010 — well before the frozen revision's date, and in any case only for the non-convex, non-necessarily-planar version. The current Wikipedia article on greedy embedding states plainly that the strong (convex) conjecture 'remains unproven,' and its most recent citation on that specific question is from 2016 (self-approaching/increasing-chord drawings). I searched broadly for any 2024–2026 work bearing on the convex/planar version specifically — arXiv listings, general web search, and the article itself — and found nothing that engages the strong conjecture as stated. Several tangential items turned up and were checked and ruled out: (1) a 2020 paper (arXiv:2003.00556, 'On the Area Requirements of Planar Greedy Drawings of Triconnected Planar Graphs,' by Cao/Strelzoff/Sun and later authors) on area bounds for the non-convex planar greedy drawing question — predates the window and concerns a different (non-convex) variant; (2) a TU Delft bachelor's thesis by Lune van Santvoord, 'Embedding polyhedral graphs' (defended 27 August 2025) — an undergraduate thesis whose visible metadata indicates it is expository/survey work under a supervisor at TU Delft, with no evidence found of a new result on the strong conjecture (the PDF could not be extracted to text through available tools, so this is a partial check — see below); (3) arXiv:2507.04538 ('Decremental Greedy Polygons and Polyhedra Without Sharp Angles' by David Eppstein) — confirmed via direct fetch to be an unrelated computational-geometry paper (max-min-angle polygons/polyhedra), sharing vocabulary ('greedy', 'polyhedra') but not addressing graph embeddings; (4) various graph-neural-network papers on 'convex constraints' and 'greedy' coreset/heuristic selection — confirmed unrelated, using the same words in a machine-learning sense with no connection to greedy graph embeddings; (5) general LLM-for-graph-problems surveys — no mention of this conjecture. No AI system was found anywhere near the actual strong conjecture. This matches the triage's 'none' verdict; I do not disagree with it, though I was unable to fully read the 2025 Delft thesis's contents (extraction blocked), which is the one loose end in an otherwise thorough negative search.
competing_reading: If the unreadable 2025 TU Delft bachelor's thesis in fact contains a new partial or full result on the strong conjecture rather than being purely expository, the status could move to `partial` or higher. Nothing in the available metadata (title, committee, thesis type, timeline) suggests this — bachelor's theses in this area are conventionally surveys or minor extensions, not conjecture-resolving contributions — but the content itself was not verified.
what_would_settle_it: Successfully extracting and reading the full text of the van Santvoord thesis (repository.tudelft.nl, file File_ae8f2fd8-1834-47b1-acb6-186bf21a5cea) to confirm it is expository and states no new result on the strong/convex conjecture; alternatively, a citation search (Google Scholar / Semantic Scholar) for any paper citing this thesis or independently claiming progress on the convex greedy embedding conjecture after January 2024.
